methodological_rigor.justification: The systematic review was prospectively registered (PROSPERO CRD420251108271) and followed PRISMA guidance, with four databases searched to July 2025, dual independent screening, and formal quality assessment using NOS and MINORS. Random-effects models with I2 heterogeneity quantification, Egger's/Begg's publication bias tests, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were applied appropriately. Important methodological concerns: no randomized controlled trials were included, language was restricted to English despite an initial no-language-restriction claim, 9 of 20 candidate full-texts were excluded for 'full-text unavailability' (a retrieval failure indicator), and 2- and 3-year OS estimates are derived from single studies but still presented as pooled results with CIs. Meta-regression to explain I2 up to 92% was not performed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies (single-arm trials and retrospective cohorts; no RCTs), this corresponds to Oxford LoE 2a. The topic is highly clinically relevant because high-risk B-ALL has limited effective options, and synthesized efficacy (CR 87%, MRD negativity 81%) directly informs treatment choice especially in settings without CAR-T access. Findings provide near-term practical guidance on blinatumomab combination strategies (TKI vs chemotherapy backbone, first-line vs R/R timing) with direct translational relevance.

reporting_quality.justification: The review is PRISMA-compliant in structure: registered protocol, defined PICO, search strategy disclosed, PRISMA flow in Figure 1, quality assessment reported in Table II, and publication bias evaluated. Random-effects rationale is stated per Cochrane Handbook. Minor gaps: no PRISMA checklist reference or supplementary file, no a priori protocol deviations disclosed, the 'no language restriction' statement in search but English-only in inclusion criterion is inconsistent, and extraction of 2- and 3-year OS 'pooled' from single studies is potentially misleading. Data are summarized in tables; raw extracted data availability is not explicitly stated.

novelty_literature.justification: Several recent meta-analyses on blinatumomab in ALL already exist (including ones cited here: Marrapodi 2022 pediatric safety; Liu 2023 R/R efficacy), so the incremental contribution is specifically focusing on combination-therapy regimens in high-risk B-ALL with subgroup analyses by TKI vs chemotherapy and first-line vs R/R. This represents an incremental refinement of well-established evidence rather than a novel question or method. The subgroup analysis of CMR and the stratified safety analysis offer moderate added value.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally well organized and readable with IMRaD structure and clear tables/figures referenced. However, several numerical inconsistencies exist: abstract reports neutropenia 38% but text says 39%; the text reports grade >=3 CRS 1.6% then later 2.1%; the 3-year OS is reported as 52% (95% CI 36-66%) though Results say data from single studies; some references are concatenated without clear formatting (e.g., references 1-55). The Discussion is thorough but repetitive in places.

key_strengths: PROSPERO pre-registration (CRD420251108271) and PRISMA-aligned conduct across four databases with dual independent screening
Clinically relevant synthesis of 11 studies (402 patients) addressing high-risk B-ALL where blinatumomab-based combinations are an emerging standard
Pre-specified subgroup analyses by combination backbone (TKI vs chemotherapy), Ph status, and treatment setting (first-line vs R/R) with sensitivity and publication-bias assessment
Useful safety stratification showing 99% all-grade AE in chemotherapy-combo vs 73% in TKI-combo, informing backbone selection
key_concerns: No RCTs included; pooled estimates mix single-arm and retrospective cohort studies with high heterogeneity (I2 up to 92%)
9 of 20 full texts excluded for 'unavailability', plus English-only inclusion, substantially risks retrieval/language bias despite the stated no-language-restriction search
2- and 3-year OS estimates are from single studies yet presented as pooled meta-analytic estimates with 95% CIs, which is misleading
Significant publication bias detected for CR outcome (Egger P=0.02) without adjustment (e.g., trim-and-fill)
Numerical inconsistencies between abstract and text (e.g., neutropenia 38% vs 39%; grade >=3 CRS 1.6% vs 2.1%)
Limited novelty given recent overlapping meta-analyses in blinatumomab/B-ALL
chief_reviewer.rationale: A PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis on a clinically important topic with useful subgroup analyses but notable methodological issues including no RCTs, high heterogeneity, single-study 'pooled' long-term survival, and detected publication bias for the primary outcome. A Tier 3 hematology or oncology journal is the highest plausible venue with major revisions to correct pooling of single-study estimates, address publication bias, and resolve numerical inconsistencies.
